wrong_idea: It copied a page that was later deleted from the internet
correction: The link never existed: the chatbot wrote text that looked like a citation.

wrong_idea: Its links are tested before you see them, so the site is down for now
correction: Nothing is tested: without a search it writes link-shaped text; with a search, open the page and check it says what was claimed.

wrong_idea: It made up the link deliberately, to hide that it didn't know
correction: There is no intent: an invented link is just plausible-looking text.

wrong_idea: A chatbot sounds sure once it has checked the facts behind it
correction: It sounds sure either way; its tone isn't a check.

wrong_idea: Confident wording means the answer came from a trusted source
correction: The wording comes from how it writes, not from where the facts came from.

wrong_idea: When a chatbot is unsure of a fact, it tells you before it answers
correction: Chatbots often don't flag uncertainty; check the claim yourself.

wrong_idea: A chatbot checks the live internet for news before it answers you
correction: Only with a web search tool switched on; otherwise it uses its training text.

wrong_idea: Chatbots are retrained on the news overnight, so they stay up to date
correction: Its training stops at a date; later events aren't in it.

wrong_idea: If its data were out of date, the chatbot would refuse to answer
correction: It usually answers anyway; it may not know its data is old.

wrong_idea: It changed the answer because it has now checked the facts properly
correction: Pushback alone can change it, with no new checking.

wrong_idea: A chatbot switches answers once it works out the new one is right
correction: It can switch a right answer to a wrong one to agree with you; check against the notes.

wrong_idea: Disagreeing makes it go and look up a more reliable source
correction: Disagreeing doesn't make it search; check against the notes.
